name: OpenSpec
description: Spec-driven development (SDD) for AI coding assistants.
one_liner: A tool that makes an AI coding assistant write down exactly what it's about to build and get approval before it writes any code, so you don't end up with a feature you didn't ask for.
buyer: A non-technical startup founder or product manager who directs AI-built features but keeps getting surprised by what the AI actually shipped.
business_use_cases: A solo founder building their product with AI assistance uses it to review a plain-English spec before code gets written, catching misunderstandings early and cheaply.
An agency uses it to create a client-approvable spec document as a billable milestone before any AI-assisted development work begins.
A product manager team standardizes on it so every AI-built feature has a paper trail of what was intended versus built, useful for audits and handoffs.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a 'spec-first AI development' service where you write and get sign-off on specs, then build, billed per milestone
Build a hosted spec-review dashboard for teams to track and approve AI-generated specs, sold per seat

steal_this: This weekend, offer a fixed-price 'spec sprint': turn a founder's vague feature idea into an approved spec document they can hand to any developer or AI tool.
